content.text:
Yes, one thing, from the files in this project. I can't see anything about library prep or run batches, so that part is open.

**Lane is partly lined up with condition.** Each sample was sequenced on only one lane (from `files.csv`):

| Condition | Samples (lane) |
|---|---|
| control | S1 (L002), S2 (L001), S3 (L002) |
| treated | S4 (L001), S5 (L001), S6 (L002) |

The conditions are not fully confounded with lane, because both span L001 and L002. But the split is lopsided in opposite directions: control has 2 of 3 on L002, and treated has 2 of 3 on L001. If the two lanes differ systematically, a lane effect could be partly read as a treatment effect. That is only a risk if the lanes carried different libraries or runs. If all six libraries were pooled and run across both lanes, lane is a minor technical factor. Samples that each sit on a single lane are less typical of one shared pool, but the filenames can't tell me which case this is.

**The design table has nowhere to record it.** `rnaseq_bulk_design.csv` has only `sample_id, condition, group, replicate`. A formula in stage 02 can only use those columns, so it can't adjust for lane or any other batch.

The rest of the design is simple. It has 3 vs 3 replicates and one factor, and `condition` and `group` are identical. Nothing else in the design changes how to read the comparison. With n=3 per arm the test has modest power, so a non-significant gene isn't evidence of no change.

If you know the lanes or libraries differ, say so before you sign off. I can't add a batch column to the design table or to `samples.csv`, because stage 01 doesn't allow that. Otherwise the samplesheet is correct as written.

I'm still waiting on your sign-off, or on a word to start stage 02 for rnaseq_bulk.
